gaps.sentence: He stopped ___ coffee before bed and now sleeps much better.
gaps.explanation: 'Stop doing' = quit the activity; 'stop to drink' would mean pause in order to drink.

gaps.sentence: They're planning ___ the flat before selling it.
gaps.explanation: plan + to-infinitive (plan on + -ing also occurs informally): planning to redecorate.

gaps.sentence: It started ___ just as we left the house.
gaps.explanation: start/begin take either -ing or to-infinitive; with continuous or states, 'to' is preferred. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: My boss won't ___ me take Friday off.
gaps.explanation: let + object + bare infinitive: won't let me take. (allow/permit take to: allow me to take.)
pretend + to-infinitive; negative: not to hear.

gaps.sentence: She suggested ___ the meeting until Monday.
When I was a student, I used ___ in shared flats.
gaps.explanation: used TO + infinitive = past habit/state: used to live. (Compare: be used to living.)
